source.title: Improving LLM Unlearning Robustness via Random Perturbations
source.authors: Dang Huu-Tien; Hoang Thanh-Tung; Anh Bui; Minh-Phuong Nguyen; Le-Minh Nguyen; Naoya Inoue

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some appendix results are shown only in figures, and Table 4's flattened layout makes detailed assignment of some values uncertain.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests recovery and robustness using its own relearning and white-box attack experiments, rather than reproducing the specific original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports experiments on RNA's robustness to forget-tokens in retain-queries. Those results address retain-robustness, not recovery of targeted knowledge, so they are not cataloged as claim-version rows. Hyperparameter grid-search values are not results rows.
record.test_reason: The study unlearns WMDP knowledge from Zephyr-7B with 9 RM/PO methods, with and without RNA. It then runs its own recovery attacks on WMDP QA accuracy: relearning on forget-samples (Figs 4–5), benign Wikitext fine-tuning (Fig 11), and logitlens, orthogonalization, Enhanced GCG and set-difference pruning (Table 4). These are its own methods aimed at the same question, so T2. Its main subject is retain-robustness, which is off-claim apart from showing a cost to general ability.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that unlearning acts like a self-inflicted backdoor: it hides and redirects target knowledge rather than erasing it, and makes models fragile to forget-tokens in retain-queries. RNA improves this retain-robustness while keeping forget/retain accuracy. In ablations RNA does not consistently change robustness to white-box recovery attacks and makes relearning and benign fine-tuning recover knowledge faster.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates established unlearning methods and adds Random Noise Augmentation; it does not reproduce the original studies' recovery protocols as a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery results vary by unlearning method and attack setting. The paper reports that RNA's effect on white-box recovery attacks is not consistent; relearning behavior and RNA noise scale also vary.

fits_no_version.finding: RNA models relearn faster after forget-sample relearning and recover more after benign Wikitext fine-tuning than the original unlearned models. Under white-box attacks RNA is inconsistent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent-noise smoothing added for retain-robustness increases an unlearned model's susceptibility to relearning.

record.problems: Several relevant recovery results are figure-only. The paper states that experiments are limited to 7B or 8B models and selected layer parameters; it also notes that RNA depends heavily on hyperparameter grid search. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the recovery results.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed method-by-method numerical rows for orthogonalization and Enhanced GCG in Appendix D.3, Table 4 were not extracted because the flattened table layout makes some values difficult to assign confidently. Other white-box attack values in Table 4 are likewise omitted. Figure-specific method and sample-count values for Figures 4, 5, and 11 are not transcribed; the rows above preserve only the accompanying textual findings.

untested.parts: Quantization is cited only (Zhang et al. 2025), not tested.
Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information are not tested; only the optimized-prefix Enhanced GCG is.
No method here claims forget-robustness. RNA targets retain-robustness, and its forget-robustness comparison is an ablation.
Loosely related relearning sets are not tested. Only the forget-set subsets (n=5–1000) and unrelated Wikitext are.

missing.what: Per-method, per-attack WMDP accuracy under logitlens, orthogonalization, Enhanced GCG and pruning for original unlearned models, against the default and base (44.3 cyber / 64.5 bio)
Default WMDP (~24–29) and MMLU (~53–57 vs 58.4) of original unlearned models, showing near-chance forgetting with retained ability
Perturbed-MMLU accuracy reduction from a single forget-token (RM avg 23.3%, PO avg 43.3%)

record.verdict_notes: Several labels rest on text not captured by rows: the Table 4 values and the perturbed-MMLU drops. Table 4's flattened layout was read as Cyber: Default, Logitlens, Ortho, E.GCG, Pruning, then Bio: Default, Ortho, E.GCG, Pruning. The second half has the column order reversed. Chance on WMDP is 25%. Main recovery results are Zephyr-7B only. The reader's V-ids are invalid; map V1→A, V2→B, V6→F. F was dropped from the rows because RNA is not presented as a forget-robust method.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports targeted-knowledge accuracy and attack results, but does not establish that all methods bring targeted accuracy to near chance while preserving general ability under every attack setting.
The paper tests Wikitext fine-tuning and small sets of forget-samples; it does not establish recovery from loosely related examples generally.

The study evaluates orthogonalization, but detailed method-by-method values from Table 4 are not extracted here. Its claim that unlearning hides rather than erases is also presented as a proposed mechanism, not a direct weight-level deletion test.
Quantization is cited as prior work; the authors do not test it.

The study evaluates Enhanced GCG, but detailed method-by-method values from Table 4 are not extracted here. It does not test rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information as recovery attacks.
RNA is evaluated against relearning and white-box recovery attacks, but not quantization. Results do not demonstrate consistent resistance to all attack types.

relation.reason: Its own recovery results bear on versions A, B, C and E.

tranche.reason: It runs Łucki et al.'s recovery attacks (relearning, Wikitext fine-tuning, orthogonalization, Enhanced GCG, pruning, logit lens) on unlearned Zephyr-7B models. These differ from the originals' probes and GCG. Łucki is a challenge source, not an original, so T2 fits.

source_check.notes: Table 4 is garbled by extraction but can be parsed: the top half is attacks with the Cyber forget-set, the bottom half with the Bio forget-set. The logit lens is last-layer only, so it adds nothing beyond the default evaluation. Relearning and Wikitext results are figure-only and merge original and RNA models. R5 duplicates R1/R2.

statements.correction: 2501.19202, Zephyr-7B-β, 9 RM/PO methods: LoRA relearning (3 epochs) on n=5–1000 WMDP forget-set samples. Fig 4/5 captions say this restores the unlearned domain and also recovers the other domain. No numbers in the text. There is no held-out-facts split.
statements.problem: The statement gives nothing specific for this study. Its R3 relearns on WMDP forget-corpus documents and scores on the WMDP QA set, which is not a held-out-facts split. Only the cross-domain recovery is held-out-like. Values are figure-only.

statements.correction: 2501.19202, Zephyr-7B-β, 9 RM/PO methods, LoRA fine-tuning on Wikitext retain-samples: original and RNA models 'remain substantially below the base model'. RNA models recover more WMDP accuracy than the originals. Figure-only (Fig 11). The amount of recovery is not stated.
statements.problem: Puts this study under a 'no or weak recovery' (challenges) heading. The text only says models stay substantially below base after Wikitext fine-tuning. It gives no values before fine-tuning, and RNA models recover more. The study's verdict for this condition is limits_scope (incomplete recovery), not challenges.
Matches the text. Minor: R2 is WMDP-Cyber and both rows cover 9 RM/PO methods, under an 'RMU, WMDP-Bio' heading. differences_stated notes the aggregation and the merging of original and RNA models.

statements.correction: 2501.19202 applies the logit lens only at the last layer (≈ model output). WMDP accuracy stays at default (~27–28, e.g. RMU Cyber 28.6→28.6), so this can't show whether access is blocked. In the same study, orthogonalization takes RMU Bio 28.0→64.0 (base 64.5).
statements.problem: The numbers are right (original models: logit lens 26.6–28.6 Cyber, 27.0–28.3 Bio; RMU Cyber 28.6 vs default 28.6). But the logit lens is applied only at the last layer, which is the model's own output with an instruction prefix. So it cannot detect retained access and is not evidence that readouts find little.

statements.correction: 2501.19202, Zephyr-7B RMU: logit lens only at the last layer (≈ output), 27.7 Bio / 28.6 Cyber vs default 28.0 / 28.6. In the same study, orthogonalization (an intervention) takes RMU Bio 28.0→64.0 and Cyber 28.6→39.8 (base 64.5 / 44.3).
statements.problem: The RMU logit-lens values are right (Bio 27.7 vs default 28.0; Cyber 28.6 vs 28.6). But a last-layer logit lens is the model's output, not an internal readout, so it doesn't belong on the 'readouts' side of a readout-vs-intervention contrast.
Table 4: Enhanced GCG on Cyber QA is 25.3–32.6 for original models (26.3–32.5 with the Bio forget-set; RNA up to 32.3). Default is 23.9–28.9 and base 44.3. The largest gain is Adaptive RMU 27.9→32.6.
Bio forget-set attack: NPO+MSE 27.0→52.9 and Adaptive RMU 29.4→43.9 match Table 4 (base 64.5). Cyber GCG stays ~25–33 against base 44.3.
